tldr: By leveraging knowledge from World Action Models (WAMs) pre-trained on tabletop manipulation and introducing arm-manipulability-aware whole-body coordination alongside a unified controller representation (UWBC), this study achieves highly accurate humanoid loco-manipulation without learning whole-body behavior from scratch.
hero_caption: Overall architecture of WholeBodyWAM. On the left, a shared Diffusion Transformer (DiT) concurrently generates future visual dynamics, manipulation actions, and UWBC commands. On the right, the Coordination-Aware Self-Attention (CASA) mechanism detects drops in arm manipulability to strengthen whole-body coordination.
overview:
World Action Models (WAMs), which simultaneously predict future camera observations and robot actions, have gained significant attention as a promising path toward general-purpose robot manipulation. However, most prior WAM studies have been confined to tabletop robot arms, leaving bipedal humanoid loco-manipulation largely unexplored. In humanoids, coordinating arm tasks with full-body locomotion is remarkably complex. Furthermore, the physical semantics of commands vary wildly across whole-body controllers (WBCs), and full-body humanoid demonstration data is exceedingly scarce.

To tackle this, the authors hypothesized: instead of overwriting the rich manipulation priors already embedded in pre-trained WAMs, why not structurally add WBC-grounded coordination rules? The proposed WholeBodyWAM preserves the pre-trained WAM backbone while concurrently predicting full-body control commands as a separate stream. It introduces a common interface called UWBC to absorb differences across diverse WBCs, as well as an attention mechanism named CASA that encourages full-body motion whenever the arms experience reachability limits.

Evaluations across a simulator (SIMPLE) and a real-world platform (Unitree G1) demonstrate an overall simulation success rate of 91.9%, substantially outperforming conventional WAM and Vision-Language-Action (VLA) baselines. In addition, when switching among three different WBCs, success-rate variance drops by roughly 70%. In out-of-distribution (OOD) real-world tests, the humanoid exhibited adaptive behaviors such as stepping forward autonomously to grasp a distant object after an initial miss. This work demonstrates a viable path toward scaling humanoid intelligence by grounding and extending pre-trained arm manipulation priors rather than relearning full-body behavior from scratch.
contributions: Proposed WholeBodyWAM, a world action model that preserves pre-trained manipulation priors while achieving unified whole-body control.

Constructed the Unified WBC (UWBC) interface, which decouples shared physical-semantic slots from controller-specific slots to facilitate easy adaptation across heterogeneous whole-body controllers (WBCs).

Developed Coordination-Aware Self-Attention (CASA), an attention mechanism that detects drops in directional task manipulability and adaptively amplifies information flow from manipulation to whole-body control.

Demonstrated superior task success rates, cross-WBC transferability, and out-of-distribution generalization compared to existing WAM and VLA baselines across 6 simulation tasks and 8 real-world tasks.

sections.heading: How to Solve Humanoid Whole-Body Coordination Without Starting from Scratch?
sections.summary: Humanoid loco-manipulation faces three major hurdles: the complexity of whole-body coordination, heterogeneous WBC specifications, and the scarcity of whole-body data. This study tackles these challenges by leveraging pre-trained tabletop WAM priors through structured WBC grounding and coordination mechanisms.
sections.details:
WAMs that jointly learn future visual dynamics and robot actions have shown strong potential for general-purpose robot manipulation. However, extending them to humanoid loco-manipulation—where a bipedal robot must coordinate its entire body while interacting with its environment—remains largely uncharted territory.

There are three core reasons for this gap. First is the complexity of whole-body coordination. Beyond moving the end-effectors to manipulate objects, the robot must decide when and how to coordinate its torso and legs. Second is the heterogeneity of whole-body controllers (WBCs). Existing WBCs take vastly different command types: some expect joint angles, while others take center-of-mass velocities or foot contact states, resulting in fragmented physical semantics. Third is the scarcity of humanoid demonstration data. While single-arm data is abundant, collecting high-quality whole-body humanoid demonstrations is extremely costly and rare.

Prior approaches typically either force-expand the action dimensions of existing models and fine-tune them, or train a monolithic whole-body policy from scratch. However, the former only implicitly learns controller semantics and often causes task failure, while the latter demands massive amounts of full-body data and remains locked to a single specific controller.

To overcome these issues, the authors designed WholeBodyWAM to preserve pre-trained end-effector priors while structurally adding controller grounding and coordination. The architecture rests on three pillars: a structured formulation that decouples manipulation and whole-body control streams, a unified WBC interface (UWBC), and an attention mechanism (CASA) that assists the arms based on manipulability limits.

sections.heading: At the Intersection of World Models and Humanoid Control
sections.summary: This section reviews video-diffusion-based World Action Models (WAMs) alongside reinforcement learning and imitation learning for humanoid whole-body control. WholeBodyWAM stands out by introducing shared semantics and coordination mechanisms that bridge the gap between high-level priors and heterogeneous low-level controllers.
sections.details:
### II-A World Action Models
Models that unify video prediction and action generation, such as DreamZero, Cosmos Policy, and Fast-WAM (which discards future visual tokens during inference), have emerged recently. Humanoid extensions have also surfaced, including DiT4DiT for bimanual manipulation, and MotionWAM or $\omega$-0 for predicting whole-body motion latents. Nonetheless, these works either merely widen the action space or retrain policies from scratch exclusively for humanoids. In contrast, WholeBodyWAM preserves pre-trained WAM manipulation priors and focuses on efficiently learning controller grounding and coordination from limited humanoid data.

### II-B Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
In low-level whole-body motor control, robust WBC frameworks such as OmniH2O, HOVER, and HugWBC have been established to reliably track external commands. Built upon these controllers, Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models such as WholeBodyVLA, $\Psi_0$, HEX, and OpenHLM learn high-level autonomous behaviors. However, most existing methods lock their action representations to a single controller's specifications. WholeBodyWAM differs fundamentally by learning shared semantics across multiple WBCs via UWBC, acquiring grounded representations that transfer cleanly across different controllers.

sections.heading: WholeBodyWAM: Decouple, Unify, and Coordinate
sections.summary: Extending a pre-trained DiT, the framework simultaneously generates three streams: future video, arm manipulation, and whole-body control. The core innovations include the 'UWBC' slot design that unifies disparate WBC interfaces and 'CASA', which dynamically adjusts attention weights based on task-directional manipulability.
sections.details:
### III-A Problem Formulation
Humanoid loco-manipulation is formulated as the joint prediction of future visual dynamics $\mathbf{v}$, arm manipulation actions $\mathbf{m}$, and whole-body control commands $\mathbf{u}$, conditioned on a context $\mathbf{c}_t$ consisting of visual history $\mathbf{o}_{0:t}$, current robot state $\mathbf{s}_{t}$, and language instruction $\ell$.

### III-B Model Architecture
The backbone builds on the video Diffusion Transformer (DiT) from DreamZero. It consumes language embeddings from a pre-trained T5, visual tokens from a Wan video VAE, and state representations from a lightweight robot state encoder. Target predictions are split into three typed token streams—visual $\mathbf{v}$, manipulation $\mathbf{m}$, and whole-body control $\mathbf{u}$—and jointly denoised using flow matching across shared DiT blocks. The objective balances prediction errors across streams with weighting coefficients $\lambda_k$.

### III-C Unified WBC Interface (UWBC)
Concatenating heterogeneous controller commands into a single flat vector causes models to overfit to specific WBC variants. UWBC addresses this by clearly separating shared semantic slots (46 dimensions) that have consistent physical meaning across controllers from controller-specific residual slots (10 dimensions). Shared slots comprise task-space commands such as base velocities and torso poses (16 dimensions), along with target joint positions and velocities for the lower body and waist (15 dimensions each, totaling 30 dimensions). For any downstream WBC, only corresponding active slots are engaged, while undefined slots are masked out.

### III-D Coordination-Aware Self-Attention (CASA)
When a task can be solved using arms alone, full-body motion is unnecessary; however, when arms reach their mechanical limits, torso and leg coordination must kick in. CASA governs this mathematically. First, it estimates the task progression direction vector $\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{a,t}$ from recent end-effector velocity, and computes the task-directional manipulability $c_{a,t}$ using a joint-limit-penalized manipulability matrix. By comparing $c_{a,t}$ against reference upper bounds $c^{\mathrm{ref}}_{a,t}$ from a pre-computed voxel map, the model determines manipulability drop rates. Taking the worst drop between both arms yields a coordination gate $g_t \in [0, 1]$. Using $g_t$, DiT self-attention adaptively injects a logit bias into the attention weights where UWBC queries attend to manipulation keys. As a result, whole-body assistance is strongly recruited only when the arms run out of operational margin.

Right: The CASA pipeline, which derives a gate value $g_t$ from end-effector task manipulability and injects an attention bias from manipulation to UWBC tokens.

sections.heading: Evaluations in Sim and Real: High Success Rates and OOD Adaptability
sections.summary: Comprehensive experiments were conducted on a real Unitree G1 robot and in the SIMPLE simulator. The method achieved an overall simulation success rate of 91.9%, drastically curtailed performance variance across different WBCs, and demonstrated emergent recovery behaviors in real-world out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios.
sections.details:
### IV-A Experimental Setup
Starting from a pre-trained 14B WAM, the model was fine-tuned using LoRA (rank=4) on 15K episodes of whole-body teleoperation demonstrations collected via a PICO 4 Ultra VR setup and retargeted to the G1 humanoid. The real robot is a Unitree G1 equipped with BrainCo Revo 2 hands and three RealSense cameras (one head-mounted, two wrist-mounted). Metrics include task success rate (TSR), intermediate task progress (TP), and cross-WBC variance (pp$^2$) to assess consistency across controllers.

### IV-B Simulation Evaluation
Across 6 tasks in the SIMPLE benchmark, WholeBodyWAM achieved an average TSR of 91.9%. It significantly outperformed DreamZero-PT (73.6%), Cosmos-3 (86.3%), and the humanoid VLA model $\Psi_0$ (82.2%) trained on the identical dataset. On tasks requiring heavy loco-manipulation coordination, such as PickBetweenTables, WholeBodyWAM led Cosmos-3 by more than 10 percentage points. Furthermore, when evaluated across three distinct WBCs (SONIC, AMO, and GEAR), WholeBodyWAM recorded an average TSR of 89.2% with a variance of 10.5 pp$^2$, slashing cross-controller performance variance by roughly 70% compared to Cosmos-3 (80.2% / 35.0 pp$^2$).

### IV-C Real-Robot Evaluation
Across 8 diverse real-world tasks on the Unitree G1, WholeBodyWAM attained an in-distribution (ID) success rate of 81.3% (vs. 57.5% for DreamZero) and maintained 68.8% under out-of-distribution (OOD) conditions with modified object layouts and instructions (vs. 40.0% for DreamZero). Notably, in an OOD towel-hanging trial where the rack was moved 10 cm further away, the robot missed its initial grasp, spontaneously stepped forward, twisted its torso to extend reach, and successfully grabbed the towel on the second attempt. This recovery was never present in the training demonstrations, highlighting emergent coordination arising from grounding manipulation priors into whole-body control.

### IV-D Ablation Study
Ablation experiments (Table II) show that removing CASA causes average TSR to drop to 86.9% (-5.0 points). Removing UWBC to predict SONIC commands directly lowers TSR to 84.7% (-7.2 points), while merging all actions into a single monolithic vector degrades performance to 80.8% (-11.1 points). These results validate that structurally decoupling manipulation from whole-body control, unifying physical semantics, and dynamically coordinating based on manipulability are all essential.

captions.F6: Snapshots of 8 real-world tasks executed on the Unitree G1 robot. Tasks range from arm-centric manipulation (watering plants, wiping tables) to demanding whole-body coordination involving extended walking and deep squatting (carrying baskets, moving boxes, opening and traversing doors).
captions.F8: Emergent recovery via whole-body coordination under out-of-distribution (OOD) placement. After missing the towel because it was placed 10 cm too far, the robot autonomously steps forward and rotates its torso to extend reaching distance, successfully grasping it on the second try.

sections.heading: Takeaway: Structurally Bridging Arm Intelligence to Legged Mobility
sections.summary: WholeBodyWAM enables humanoid loco-manipulation by combining pre-trained WAM manipulation knowledge with structured UWBC and CASA mechanisms. It charts a scalable course for humanoid development: grounding and expanding existing arm intelligence to controllers rather than relearning whole-body behaviors from scratch.
sections.details:
This paper presented WholeBodyWAM, a WBC-grounded World Action Model for humanoid loco-manipulation. By preserving pre-trained visual and manipulation priors, unifying heterogeneous whole-body controller semantics through UWBC, and adaptively gating whole-body coordination via CASA, the framework bridges high-level reasoning with low-level execution.

Both simulation and real-world experiments confirmed superior task performance, robust OOD generalization, and remarkable cross-controller portability over competitive baselines. Data scaling analyses further validated that structured reuse enables highly sample-efficient learning on limited task-specific demonstrations.

The core takeaway of this research is clear: humanoid whole-body intelligence does not necessitate relearning full-body motor behaviors from scratch on massive datasets. Structurally connecting vast pre-trained world-action knowledge to low-level controllers through standardized interfaces and physics-grounded coordination provides a practical, scalable blueprint for humanoid intelligence.

takeaways: Pre-trained World Action Models (WAMs) from tabletop setups can be efficiently adapted to humanoid loco-manipulation by structurally decoupling and adding a whole-body control output stream without disrupting existing weights.

Decoupling heterogeneous WBC commands into shared physical-semantic slots (46D) and controller-specific residual slots (10D) via UWBC markedly improves robustness against changes in underlying controllers.
Incorporating task-directional manipulability as an attention bias gate (CASA) triggers emergent whole-body coordination and recovery behaviors whenever the arms encounter reachability limits.
limitations: Mapping and masking configurations for UWBC slots must still be manually defined and registered for each downstream WBC.

Task direction estimation relies on end-effector displacement vectors from recent steps, which may lead to unstable coordination gating when the arm is stationary or undergoing rapid directional reversals.
Fine-tuning and simulation data collection still require around 15K whole-body teleoperation demonstrations, meaning the framework is not entirely zero-shot adaptable to new humanoid platforms.
